- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.67) in the recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) in recent history, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast baseline or add downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” correction to prevent overextension.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for first 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., rapid drop after peak), model often fails to recognize it — add a “reversion buffer” to forecast, especially if sentiment is mixed or declining.
- When sentiment history shows a clear trend (e.g., rising from 0.33 to 1.00), model may lag in adjusting — apply a “sentiment lag correction” to align forecast with sentiment shift.
